I've been drilling down on the nuances of 8 placement, using train 5 and 7 as my primary guides. It seems adjacent 1s, in the same row or column, dictate the insertion of 8s. Now, I'm confident I've cracked the core logic. A cell transforms to an 8 if it's a 0 and flanked by 1s, either horizontally or vertically, even if they aren't adjacent. I've formulated a solid rule: a cell (r, c) becomes an 8 if it's 0, and either a row r contains 1s to its left and right, or a column c contains 1s above and below. I've confirmed that this doesn't overwrite any 1s! The algorithm now targets finding the minimum and maximum indices of 1s in each row and column. Any 0 between them, becomes an 8.
